title: Equipment Master
context: Plant Maintenance › Preventive & Breakdown Maintenance (PM) › Equipment Master

cards.title: Where the Equipment Master sits in the maintenance architecture
cards.body:
The Equipment Master is step two in the preventive maintenance setup workflow within Plant Maintenance.
It follows Permit Master where safety templates and isolation rules are established for plant operations.
Maintenance planners use this screen to register every piece of machinery, vehicle, and installed tool.
It establishes the definitive asset entity upon which all maintenance orders and service calls are built.
The next operational steps are raising maintenance requests and scheduling periodic overhauls.
Equipment records link to physical factory locations, designated custodians, work centers, and operators.
Bill of materials sections define standard engineering spares required for routine overhauls.
Every maintenance request, work order, and breakdown log requires a valid equipment reference.
Accurate equipment data ensures that machine histories, running hours, and repair costs remain auditable.
This screen provides the operational foundation for enterprise asset reliability management across sites.
Physical verification against this document ensures company equipment registers match physical floor assets.
Without this master definition, engineering teams cannot schedule preventive maintenance or track machine downtime.
Maintenance histories captured here enable engineering managers to analyze equipment reliability over time.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.

cards.title: Mandatory equipment attributes, ownership classifications, and validations
cards.body:
Creating an equipment record requires critical identification, classification, and ownership inputs.
The user must enter an equipment name, serial number, and select a valid ownership category from master options.
Ownership classifications differentiate clearly between company-owned, hired, and customer equipment.
Selecting valid equipment categories and equipment types is compulsory for all registered plant assets.
If the equipment name or serial number is left blank, saving is immediately prohibited by system checks.
Custody details require a valid custodian name, contact number, and formal custody assignment date.
The year of manufacture date cannot be later than the equipment acquisition date recorded on the header.
The date of custody cannot precede the original acquisition date of the machinery under any circumstances.
Duplicate equipment names or duplicate serial numbers within the company are stopped by validation routines.
Missing mandatory headers halt saving and highlight the exact asset information requiring user entry.
These checks prevent incomplete or duplicate equipment records from contaminating asset registers.
Accurate classification ensures that maintenance schedules and financial depreciation apply appropriate rules.
Mandatory custody details establish clear operational accountability for plant equipment safety.

cards.title: Physical location tracking, division alignment, and custodian responsibilities
cards.body:
Equipment records track physical operating sites to support maintenance dispatching and inventory delivery.
The user specifies operating location, effective location date, work center, and street address details.
The operating location must match an active functional location configured in company masters.
Operating division assignments must align with the operational location of the machinery on site.
Moving equipment to another factory location requires a formal change of location entry in the system.
Assigned custodians are responsible for machinery security, operator safety, and daily upkeep.
If the custodian contact number contains invalid characters, validation blocks the save operation.
When vehicle equipment includes drivers, driver effective dates and licences are recorded for fleet management.
Accurate location tracking ensures maintenance technicians are dispatched to the right site during emergencies.
Historical location logs preserve a complete audit trail of machine relocations across factory divisions.
Correct location mapping guarantees that maintenance costs charge to the proper operational cost center.
These controls prevent machinery from operating in unapproved or unmonitored factory areas.
Custodian assignment ensures machinery is operated only by qualified and authorized personnel.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.

cards.title: Equipment bill of materials, standard spares, and life span tracking
cards.body:
The equipment record maintains a dedicated bill of materials for maintenance spares and assemblies.
Planners configure standard replacement parts, sub-assemblies, and consumable items for the asset.
Each spare line specifies the item reference, technical grade, approved make, unit, and required quantity.
Items marked for mandatory consumption entry require technicians to record serial numbers on replacement.
Life span parameters establish the expected operating hours or days before component replacement falls due.
When maintenance orders are generated, bill of materials components default automatically into job plans.
Spares configured here must exist as active items within Material Management inventory masters.
Predefined component structures accelerate emergency repair ordering and reduce machine downtime.
Accurate spares mapping ensures storekeepers stock the exact engineering parts required for overhauls.
Technicians review bill of materials specifications before disassembling complex machinery assemblies.
This standardization prevents non-standard or incompatible components from being fitted to plant machinery.
Component life span tracking enables proactive replacement before in-service mechanical failure occurs.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.
Every milestone produces an auditable record connecting original requests to final authorized financial commitments.

cards.title: Safety permit attachments, measurement parameters, and operating limits
cards.body:
High-risk equipment records link directly to mandatory safety permits and check lists in the system.
Planners attach approved work permit templates defining electrical lockout and mechanical safety rules.
Measurement sections establish operating parameters such as temperature, pressure, and vibration limits.
Each parameter defines normal operating values, alert thresholds, and daily maximum running limits.
When daily meter readings exceed defined alert thresholds, the system flags maintenance alerts for review.
Safety instructions attached to the equipment default into all future maintenance work orders.
Technicians cannot bypass safety permit requirements during hazardous overhaul operations on site.
These safety parameters protect operating personnel and prevent catastrophic equipment failures in the plant.
Historical measurement values provide predictive maintenance insights to prevent unexpected breakdowns.
Clear operating limits ensure operators shut down machinery before minor faults cause major damage.
Safety compliance records remain permanently associated with the asset for regulatory safety audits.
This integration guarantees that machinery operates strictly within certified engineering safety envelopes.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.
Every milestone produces an auditable record connecting original requests to final authorized financial commitments.

cards.title: Equipment lifecycle states, deactivation rules, and deletion restrictions
cards.body:
Equipment records remain active throughout the operational life of the machinery in the plant.
Assets taken out of service can be marked inactive to prevent new maintenance orders from being raised.
Inactive equipment records remain fully available in historical searches for regulatory and audit compliance.
An equipment record cannot be deleted if active maintenance orders or requests reference it.
If meter readings or running hours have been logged against the asset, deletion is blocked by system checks.
Open service contracts or warranty records linked to the equipment also prohibit document deletion.
Attempting to delete a referenced equipment record triggers an explicit system refusal message detailing dependencies.
These restrictions preserve equipment maintenance history and prevent orphan records in asset ledgers.
Users must decommission or retire equipment through formal disposal entries instead of deleting records.
Complete historical maintenance logs remain permanently accessible for engineering review and residual valuation.
Decommissioned records preserve parts replacement histories that inform future purchasing decisions.
This protection ensures that company asset registers remain auditable across entire equipment lifecycles.
Historical equipment data remains accessible for insurance claims and technical failure investigations.
